opts.why: Incorrect. Left/right is sagittal. Coronal is anterior/posterior. Transverse is superior/inferior.

opts.t: Both words mean equal left and right halves only
opts.why: Incorrect. Equal left/right halves is midsagittal.

opts.t: Transverse is the same as midsagittal
opts.why: Incorrect. Transverse is a cross-section into upper and lower.

q: What is the cells-to-systems order in the notes?

opts.t: 1 cells (basic unit of life) 2 tissues (similar cells) 3 organs (different tissues, specific function) 4 organ systems 5 organism (complete human body)
opts.why: Correct. That is the five-level list.

opts.t: Organs, then cells, then tissues
opts.why: Incorrect. Cells → tissues → organs → organ systems → organism.

opts.t: Organism first, then a single cell last
opts.why: Incorrect. Cells are first (basic unit of life); organism is last.

opts.t: Tissues skip cells and become systems directly
opts.why: Incorrect. Tissues are groups of similar cells; organs come next.

q: What do cells need, and how do they make energy in the notes?

opts.t: Need oxygen, glucose (sugar), water and nutrients. Oxygen + glucose → energy (ATP) + waste (CO₂ and water) + heat
opts.why: Correct. That is the energy equation given.

opts.t: Cells need only calcium from bone; no glucose
opts.why: Incorrect. Cells need oxygen, glucose, water and nutrients. Calcium storage is a skeletal function, not the cell-energy list.

opts.t: Glucose + heat → oxygen only
opts.why: Incorrect. The equation is oxygen + glucose → ATP + CO₂ + water + heat.

opts.t: ATP is listed as something cells do not use
opts.why: Incorrect. Energy is listed as ATP in that equation.

q: Why are airway, breathing, and circulation the top priorities, per these notes?

opts.t: High-energy cells (brain) die quickly without oxygen or glucose; lower-energy cells (skin) survive longer. Cells fail and die without that supply
opts.why: Correct. Key point: cells need a constant supply of oxygen and glucose to make energy. Without it they fail and die — that is why ABC is first. Do not add later chapters’ organ-system details; they are not in these notes.

opts.t: Skin dies first; the brain can wait
opts.why: Incorrect. Brain (high-energy) dies quickly; skin survives longer.

opts.t: Because the notes already cover the full respiratory and circulatory chapters
opts.why: Incorrect. This chapter is incomplete and stops after the skeletal system. Respiratory and circulatory systems are flagged as not in the notes.

opts.t: Because a later, unlisted body-system chapter in these notes requires it
opts.why: Incorrect. Later body systems are not in these notes. ABC is first because brain cells die quickly without oxygen or glucose.

q: Listed functions of the skeletal system?

opts.t: Shape and support; protect vital organs; movement (with muscles); store minerals (especially calcium); produce blood cells (bone marrow)
opts.why: Correct. Those five functions are listed. Joints and muscle-system details are not in the notes.

opts.t: Only store fat; no role in blood cells
opts.why: Incorrect. It produces blood cells in bone marrow and stores minerals (especially calcium).

opts.t: Think and pump blood as primary functions in this chapter
opts.why: Incorrect. Nervous and circulatory systems are not in these notes. Skeleton: shape/support, protect, move with muscles, store calcium, make blood.

opts.t: Digest glucose into ATP inside the marrow as the only function
opts.why: Incorrect. The ATP equation is for cells generally. Marrow’s listed job is producing blood cells.

q: How many bones in the adult skeleton, per the notes?

opts.why: Correct. Adult skeleton = 206 bones.

opts.t: 33 — that is the whole skeleton
opts.why: Incorrect. 33 is the number of vertebrae, not the whole skeleton (206).

opts.t: 14 cranial bones as listed
opts.why: Incorrect. Face is 14 bones. Cranium is listed as 4 bones (frontal, 2 parietal, occipital). Adult skeleton is 206.

opts.t: 12 — one for each rib pair only
opts.why: Incorrect. 12 pairs of ribs (24 ribs) plus 1 sternum are the thorax count. Adult total is 206.

q: Spine count in the notes?

opts.t: 33 vertebrae: cervical 7, thoracic 12, lumbar 5, sacrum 5 fused, coccyx 4 fused
opts.why: Correct. Memorize 7 / 12 / 5 / 5 fused / 4 fused.

opts.t: 26 vertebrae: 12 cervical, 7 lumbar
opts.why: Incorrect. Cervical 7, thoracic 12, lumbar 5, sacrum 5 fused, coccyx 4 fused = 33.

opts.t: Sacrum 4 fused and coccyx 5 fused
opts.why: Incorrect. Sacrum 5 fused; coccyx 4 fused.

opts.t: Thoracic 5 and lumbar 12
opts.why: Incorrect. Thoracic 12; lumbar 5.

q: What cranial and facial bones are actually named in the notes?

opts.t: Cranium (4 per the notes): frontal, parietal (2), occipital. Face (14): nasal, zygomatic (cheek), maxilla (upper jaw), mandible (lower jaw), and others not named
opts.why: Correct. Temporal and other extra skull bones are flagged as not in the notes. Do not invent them.

opts.t: The notes name more than four cranial bones
opts.why: Incorrect. Extra skull bones beyond the listed four are explicitly not in the notes. Listed cranium: frontal, 2 parietal, occipital.

opts.t: Mandible is the upper jaw and maxilla is the lower jaw
opts.why: Incorrect. Maxilla is upper jaw; mandible is lower jaw.

opts.t: Zygomatic is a vertebra in the neck
opts.why: Incorrect. Zygomatic is the cheek bone of the face. Neck vertebrae are cervical (7).

q: Which bone region do the notes say has the highest potential to bleed, and which bones are listed there?

opts.t: Pelvis — ilium, ischium, pubis (fused on each side) — highest potential to bleed (most blood)
opts.why: Correct. Appendicular also lists shoulder girdle (clavicle, scapula); upper: humerus, radius, ulna, carpals, metacarpals, phalanges; lower: femur, patella, tibia, fibula, tarsals, metatarsals, phalanges. Thorax: 12 rib pairs (24) and sternum 1.

opts.t: Cranium — frontal and occipital bleed the most in the notes
opts.why: Incorrect. The notes give highest bleed potential to the pelvis.

opts.t: Patella only — listed as most blood
opts.why: Incorrect. Patella is listed in the lower extremity, not as highest bleed. Pelvis is highest.

opts.t: Clavicle and scapula — the notes call the shoulder the highest bleed
opts.why: Incorrect. Shoulder girdle is clavicle and scapula, but highest bleed potential is the pelvis.
